sentences.text: Araripesaurus is a pterosaur, a flying reptile, belonging to the suborder Pterodactyloidea, a group characterized by more advanced flight adaptations.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of a partial wing including distal radius and ulna fragments, carpals, all metacarpals, and several digits.
This specific specimen was a subadult with an estimated wingspan of 2.2 meters.
Two other known specimens consist of wing fragments that are roughly one-third larger than the holotype.
The specific name castilhoi honors collector Moacir Marques de Castilho, who donated the fossil-bearing nodule in 1966.
Araripesaurus was discovered in the Romualdo Formation of the Santana Group in northeastern Brazil.
The genus Araripesaurus was named in 1971 by the Brazilian paleontologist Llewellyn Ivor Price, and the genus name refers to the Araripe Plateau.
Llewellyn Ivor Price originally classified Araripesaurus in the family Ornithocheiridae.
Later, Kellner classified Araripesaurus as close to Anhangueridae and more derived than Istiodactylus based on cladistic analysis.
Alexander Kellner noted that Araripesaurus resembled Anhanguera piscator in morphology but was considerably smaller.

In 1991, Alexander Kellner concluded that Araripesaurus was identical to the genus Santanadactylus, but in 2000 he reassessed the genus and concluded it could not be synonymized with Santanadactylus due to a lack of unique characters.
Araripesaurus lived during the Aptian and Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous.
A 2025 review by Pinheiro et al. suggested Araripesaurus is a nomen dubium because the specimens are insufficient for a valid diagnosis.
